CheckResult.description:
The outcome of one check for one assessment.

* ``status`` is primary.
* ``score`` (0-100) is optional; when present it must name ``score_method`` so a reader
  knows which formula produced it. No formula is agreed yet (ADR open question 2).
* ``n`` is required: the number of cases (scans) this check actually used, so thin
  evidence is visible. New checks must report their own per-check ``n`` (for example
  the cases with labels, or the AAA-positive cases for sensitivity). Only the legacy
  converter falls back to the file's scan count, because the POC never recorded it.
* ``n_effective`` (optional) is the effective sample size and must name
  ``n_effective_method`` (e.g. ``kish_design_effect_per_person``, ``cluster_icc``),
  mirroring score/score_method; ``0 < n_effective <= n``. Rationale: repeat scans of the
  same person (hospital_b has 80 scans from 40 real people) and clustering within a
  site are correlated, so they carry less information than ``n`` independent cases.
  That matters for Wilson intervals and for the "too few to judge" suppression, which
  should use the effective size, not the raw scan count.
* ``subjects`` (optional) is the number of distinct people behind the ``n`` cases, and
  ``subjects <= n``.
* ``failing_sub_factors`` must be sub-factors of the registered check, and must be empty
  when the status is ``ok``.

n.description: Cases this check actually used (per-check, not per-file).
n.title: N

VerdictOverride.description:
A human decision that replaces the derived outcome.

Overriding to ``go`` while checks are ``problem`` or not evaluated is allowed, but only
through this record, so the departure from the rule is always attributed and justified.

by.description: Who made the decision (person or committee identifier).
by.title: By

note.description: Required justification, at least 20 characters after trimming whitespace.
note.title: Note

outcome.description: The final outcome, replacing the derived one.

VerdictOverride.title: VerdictOverride

description:
A verdict with its rationale and the results it rests on.

Validated invariants (hold for any verdict, including a human override):

* ``go`` requires at least one result, every included result ``ok`` and nothing in
  ``not_evaluated``.
* ``no_go`` requires at least one ``problem``.
* check ids are unique and ``not_evaluated`` does not overlap the results.

These apply to the derived ``outcome``. ``override`` (optional) carries a human
decision. It must differ from the derived outcome, and :attr:`final_outcome` returns it.

not_evaluated.description: Checks the profile expects that produced no result.
not_evaluated.title: Not Evaluated

title: Verdict
